title: Semantic patch decomposition of reference meshes
description:
Pre-segment the Voyager reference mesh into coarse quad/Coons patches so each patch can be semantically tagged (eye socket, teeth, zygomatic arch, etc.) and color-coded. The agent then sees a labeled, low-data structural map of the reference instead of relying solely on chamfer distance + auto-tagged geometry, which is error-prone for anatomical features (e.g. agent's 'eye socket' vs. an observer's don't line up).

Candidate approaches:

1. **Skeleton-driven (Usai et al. ULPTS15)** — uses the curve skeleton we already have in Ixdar. Decomposes surface into cylinder regions (one per bone) + punctured-sphere regions (one per joint), each with a canonical quad template, stitched at 4-arc cylinder caps. Algorithm inferable from Campen 2017 STAR §7.1 since no public code exists. **Limitation: partitions along bones, not along surface features.** For a skull this gives ~skull-blob + mandible; eye sockets/teeth live inside the skull-blob and aren't separated.

2. **Feature-line / cross-field driven (QuadWild, QuadriFlow, libQEx)** — arcs naturally follow curvature ridges and valleys, so eye socket rims, tooth boundaries, and cheekbone ridges become patch borders automatically. Public C++ code available (nicopietroni/quadwild, hjwdzh/QuadriFlow, hcebke/libQEx). Better fit for anatomy.

3. **Hybrid** — Usai for gross articulated partition, then feature-aware subdivision of each region.

Related tickets: IX-19 (QuadMixer investigation).
definition-of-done: Spike writeup covering: (1) which approach best matches anatomical reference meshes we encounter in the ticket backlog; (2) license compatibility with our stack; (3) whether to wrap an existing C++ lib (via JNI/FFI/CLI) or reimplement in Java/Python; (4) patch labeling UI/workflow sketch — who tags (human, separate agent, Claude), how labels are persisted, how they're surfaced to the voyage agent; (5) prototype on one reference mesh from the backlog. Follow-up implementation tickets filed.
testing-plan: Prototype: run chosen method on a skull reference mesh, produce colored patch segmentation, manually label 3-5 patches, feed labeled patches into a voyage replication round, compare chamfer-convergence vs. baseline (no labels). Deliverable is the comparison + a recommendation to proceed or pivot.
